narrative.overview:
Paper Concepts behaves like a focused workbench inside Obsidian. It inherits the active desktop theme, uses native Obsidian controls, and keeps the content surface quiet so researchers can move from PDF import to processing records without learning a second visual language.

The visual hierarchy comes from spacing, type size, and semantic status text. Chinese labels are direct and functional; the reviewed surface is dark because the host theme is dark, but the system does not own a light or dark palette. Accent, surface, divider, and status colors remain theme variables.
keyCharacteristics: Native Obsidian desktop chrome and controls.
Theme-bound surfaces with no custom brand palette.
Compact, scannable task records with Chinese functional copy.
Flat surfaces, a dashed drop target, and thin separators.

rules.name: The Host Theme Rule
rules.body: Do not introduce project hex colors; surface, text, accent, and state color comes from Obsidian variables.

rules.name: The Functional Copy Rule
rules.body: Keep labels direct, short, and task-oriented; Chinese UI text names the action or state without promotional language.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: Convey depth with theme-owned tonal surfaces and separators; do not add project-level shadows or decorative effects.

dos: Do use native Obsidian controls and the active theme variables.
Do preserve direct Chinese labels and short status or metadata lines.
Do keep task rows flat, separated by one-pixel theme borders, with semantic status colors.
Do keep the drop target keyboard-visible with the two-pixel accent outline and three-pixel offset.
donts: Don't add a hex palette, gradients, shadows, custom fonts, or branded chrome.
Don't turn task records into floating cards; keep their transparent surface and bottom divider.
Don't replace host navigation or add a second app shell inside the plugin view.
Don't use decorative copy or status color without a state meaning.
